feed.title: Labour Codes Library: what changed
feed.subtitle: Changes in India's Labour Codes, Rules and notifications. An independent library by Vivek Chavan. Not a Government website, and not connected with any Government or Ministry.

entry.title: National Social Security Board constituted
entry.summary: The Central Government has constituted the Board for unorganised workers, for three years from publication.

entry.summary: National Social Security Board for unorganised workers constituted

entry.title: Pension Scheme: the Central Government's share
entry.summary: The Central Government's contribution to the Pension Scheme is limited to wages up to ₹15,000 a month, from 17 September 2026. The employer's share still follows the wage ceiling.

entry.title: EPF wage ceiling raised to ₹25,000 a month
entry.summary: The wage ceiling for the provident fund Chapter is now ₹25,000 a month. It replaces the ₹15,000 notified in May 2026.

entry.title: Bonus wage limits notified
entry.summary: Employees earning up to ₹21,000 a month are eligible for bonus, and bonus is worked out on ₹7,000 or the minimum wage. Both are deemed in force from 21 November 2025.

entry.title: Tribunal rules changed in the Industrial Relations Code
entry.summary: Section 44(4) and (9) were replaced by the Tribunals Reforms Act, 2026. See the before and after below.

entry.title: Provident fund, pension and insurance rates notified
entry.summary: Twelve per cent for provident fund, deemed from 21 November 2025, with some establishments left out. Eight and one-third per cent of wages goes to the Pension Fund, and the employer pays one-half per cent to the Insurance Fund.

entry.summary: Section 104(1) was replaced, and tribunals and authorities under the old Acts continue until those under the Code begin to work. In force from 21 November 2025.
